SUNDAY SYDOW. ANNIV 'Ali \ .—Tbe Wesleyan Sunday school anniversary was held on Sunday last. The Rev A Cecil Pnrher,s former minister at Penketh, and much loved by all knew him, was the preacher at both the morning and evening service. The children assembled on a platform in front of the pulpit. Their singing evinced good training and rt fledted great credit both on themselves and their conductor (Mr. George Carmenl. In the afternoon a musical service was held, Mr. C. E. N rrrr preelded. lhe choir and scholar. gave • rendering of the sacred cantata" Christ and His Soldier. " (John Farmer). SHOCKING BIaINING FATALITI".—FARIIF, Wire, DEATII.—An Inquest Wig held by Mr. T. Ridgeway on Monday on the body of Ellen Miller (43), wife of Richard Henry Miller, butcher and farmer,of Lane-end Farm,Strettoo. Acting-Sergeant Rostock, of Stratton, ..id that on going to the farm at 11.30 on Saturday night be found tte body of the deceased behind the kitchen door, the clothing having been partly atripped off The arms, fare, neck and cheek were burnt. He found the broken glses of a lamp about half-way up the stairs. The remainder of the lamp was at the bottom of the stairs. He was of opinion that deceased had gone upataire and bad dropped the glass of the himp and in trying to pick it up lvid ignited her clothes. Dr.llower said he had known the deceased for the last 25 years, and for the last five or six years she had been strongly addicted to habits of intemperance, going worse year otter year. 'The cause of death was shock from the burns, accelerated by her alcoholic habits. The bores were quite consistent wi:11 the suggested Goose of the accident The .11 returned a verdict I. accordance with the medical ev.dence.

HPLETLRY BoV SCOUTs.—The boys of No. 1 and No. 2 troops have spent a glorious week under canvas, with Scoutmesters Nash and Webb and Assistant Scoutmasters Key and Cowell', in Mr. Thomas Dutton- Done's field at Ileatley. The whole field being kindly placed at their disposal for the full week, and the , thanks of the masters, assistant masters, boys and friends are heartily given to Mr. and Mrs. Done for their kindness and valuable help. Games, drills, marching, bathing, to., have been in fell awing all week, and the boys have thoroughly enjoyed themselves and all look in the pink of condition after their pleasant week, and the Whit week camp of 1 911 will not readily be forgotten by soy one of ttem. A very appropriate wind-up to such a happy time took place on Sunday lest when nearly every member of the Scouts turned out for a Church Parade t 3 Warburton Church. Headed by the band they left the camp field at 2.30 p.m., and marched to Warburton, where, being expected, all arrangements had teen made, and after the service • splendid &dikess mainly to the Scouts wee given by the Rev. A. W. Thompeon, Rector of Chri•t Cbureh, Salford, which was greatly appriciated by the boys. Harry Birch, or Harry Smith Barnett, a tailor, who had been arrested it Shipley, near Bradford, was charged, on remand, at St. Helens, on Tuesday, with obtnining food and lodgings by false pretences, and stealing a watch end chain. The evidence was that on May 13 prisoner went to the house of a Mre. Hart, r widow, of 21, Traverse- nicest, Parr, and acid he had keen recommended to her for lodgings. Ile had a bicycle with him, and said he wail a tailor, and toe bad got a jolt at Mr. Coop's, the tailors, in Church-street, where they had given him a two hours' test to nee if be wee suitable. Ile had to commence work on Monday, the 15th. This was all false. Mrs. Hart mid it would be more con- venient if he could Come on the Monday. Birch said " I have just come front Huddersfield, a distance of slaty mile,, on any bicycle. I left home at 3 s.m., and it would snob n my going home end coming again to-morrow. It is too far, and lam tired." Mrs. Hart then asked for something in advance, and be said he would get it from the pont office on Monday morning. She believed tide, and took bias in. On Monday morn- ing In went out to go to the poet office, and disappeared. The police were informed, and a watch and ch,in belonging to another lodger, named Andrew Carney, ae mimed. Birch wes stated to he wanted at Warrington, rk- ham, Preston, Colne, Bolton, Wigan and Liverp tot, and he was sent for trial at the Assizes.

div.head: CURIOUS WARRINGTON CASE.
div.p: CURIOUS WARRINGTON CASE.
A Manager Burgles Employers' Safe JEWELLERY UP THE CHIMNEY.

A sensations' case was decided st the lioroueh Court on IVe.lnesday morning twinge Mr. J. W. Hayward (in the chair , Alderman Smethurst and Councillor Jackeon when John Stubbs, aged 20 years, of 22, Thewlis.street, Warring Lc it, was charged with stealing between Saturday (did June) and Whit Tuesday. a number of watches, rings and other articles value £2OO the property of Stubbs Stores Limited (Lovely-lane), of which firm he was the manager. Mr. I. H. Unsworth prosecuted and Mr. 1. S. Steel defended. Prisoner pleaded guilty. hfr. Unsworth said that in August 1910, the prisoner carried on business us. pawnbroker in partnership with his brother who used in the Liverpool district. Thet, got into financial difficulties and et the request of the prisoner one of their friends formed a company to purchase the business, the prisoner being appointed as manager at £2 per week. I he comp..% also gave him 22 El shares as an encouragement to di his best cod they further promised that if he did well for the ' company he would he presen'ed with some more shares, Matters went on fairly well until lest Tuesday week, when the prisoner went to the safe in the shop and in the presence of some customer. struck a theatrical I attitude and said that the avfe heti been burgled. Ile at once want a hoedown to the Police Station with the I reeult that an &Hoer went to the perm:hop and from his examination his suspicions were 11r01184,1 that every. thing was not above board. Ile reported what he had discovered and Itspect,r Williamson proceeded to the ;shop with one of the directors of the company. They made a minute elimination and the officer's suspicions woreconfirmed. There had been no' breaking in ' from outside. The satin, found intact. Prisoner was asked logo down to the policestation, and the adoption

of the bold course of charging the prisoner ith committing the burglary himself had thedesired effect Ile confessed he had taken the contents of the safe and had bidden the jewellery up the chimney. the police sulsequently secovering it there. The company had no desire to be vindictive but it was hoped that justice would he done as the offence warranted, In his speech on behalf of the prisoner, Mr Steel said that Stubbs was a young men of great ability, but bed got financially involved and on Jona 6th this idiotic idea seemed to Lave flashed across his mind. The , jewellery wss taliin out of the safe and planted up a chimney. The fern had sustained no loss and he put in • plea for lenient trettment on the ground or prisoner's previous good charnel., nnd the tect that his sot ens one more of folly than of criminal intint. Itrisoner was sent to g•ol for one month with hard labour.

div.head: GRAPPENHALL
div.p: GRAPPENHALL

Over 1,0(0 adults find over 400 children are to be catered for in this village on Coronation Day. After a I procession through the village, headed by the liorough Prize Rand, the parishionere will efijoy themselves iu Grappenhell Ilall Park, kindly lent for the occasion by Mr. F. Aylmer Frost. An exhaustive programme will furnish amusements and sports to last the whole dry. The programme of sports contains twenty events. A novel feature will be a baby snow for infants under one year old, when prizea to the value of one guinea will be given to the winner,. These prises are kindly given by Mrs. F. A. Frost. There will be cycle parade of hornorous and original characters • gentlemen's hat trimming competition a smelling competi- tion for Indira fifteen years old and over. Mr. Alfred Grout..is' Corocaticn Pierrot Troupe will gi VS numerous shows and a special show for the children. The children, by the way, will be further catered for by a money preaent,kindly given by Mr. H. T. Nicola. 'rhe committee will also present each child (under 15f, with n china Corofiation cup During the whole proceedings the 'oand will flay a variety of special selections ; and later in the evening they will play for dancing. The grounds committee till decorate a part of the village and erect a decorated archway at the entrance to the park. The whole of these events are strictly confined to the weds of Grappenhall. 'rho Rector will conduct a special service in the Church at II o'clock.

div.head: REV. W. BRACECAMPS PROTEST.
div.p: THE REV. W. BRACECAMPS PROTEST.
"The King First : God Last."

. The !the. lb. liracecemp on Sunday morning lest at St. P.l's Church made. protest regarding the arrange- ments fur Coronation Day. Taking en his tent" Fear God ; honour the King," he thern to not ice the order in which the two commandments were put. In criticiring the various Coronation festivii iea in different parts of the country, he said one could not help feeling that that order had been completely changed—it eras honour the King first and then God was put in the second place. But they had nothing to do with other tow. ; they lived in Warrington and they "Christian men and women ought to he's • voice in the matter es far es it concerned (hair own town. Where was Churchmanship put to-day ?It was ell very well Yr cry out when they board of Acts of Parliament passed against the Church, but where was Churchrnanship today ? Anywhere in the background. Some of them who rolled thermal..
